verifications.claim: Artemis II is NASA's first crewed mission of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Coming more than three years after the uncrewed Artemis I test flight, Artemis II will mark the first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit'; R3: 'Artemis II will be the first crewed mission of the Artemis programme'; R4: 'The first crewed Artemis flight'; R6: 'kicking off the first crewed mission of the agency's Artemis program'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Artemis II is the first crewed Artemis mission, following uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to send four astronauts on a 10-day flight around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'send four astronauts on a more than 600,000-mile, 10-day journey around the moon (a lunar flyby)'; R3: 'carrying four astronauts on a journey around the Moon and back... Duration: 10 days'; R4: 'MISSION DURATION 9 Days, 1 Hour, 32 Minutes' (actual, but scheduled as 10); R5: 'The 10-day mission'; R6: '10-day mission around the Moon and back'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts, 10-day duration (scheduled/planned), lunar flyby trajectory around Moon and back.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launches on the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Space Launch System (SLS), the rocket that carries the astronauts'; R3: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket will launch'; R4: 'SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R6: 'Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state SLS rocket launches Artemis II/Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA will test life support, communications, and navigation systems'; R3: 'now fitted with life support systems to keep the crew safe and healthy'; R4: 'test Orion’s systems in their intended environment'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention testing life support systems on Orion during Artemis II.
